title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction and spillover eviction priority to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Sophie Ramirez
description:
Motivation: In production we observed sustained KV cache fragmentation and frequent paging/spillover under mixed short/long-context workloads. This leads to increased GPU memory pressure and degraded p99 latency during tail-heavy sessions. This PR implements an adaptive compaction and priority-aware eviction pipeline to reduce fragmentation, defer expensive disk paging, and make spillover behavior more deterministic.

Summary of changes: Implemented an adaptive compaction pass that runs opportunistically when fragmentation crosses a tunable threshold; introduced a priority score for eviction (recency + tokencount + fragment_penalty) so large fragmented entries are targeted before many small hot entries; added background async spillover files per-shard with backpressure-aware write batching to minimize synchronous page faults; exposed config knobs for compaction threshold, eviction priority weights, and spillbackpressure watermarks; added metrics, unit/integration tests, and benchmark harness updates.

Checklist:
- [x] Core algorithm + runtime integration
- [x] Unit tests for compaction and eviction heuristics
- [x] Integration test covering mixed short/long context workload with simulated memory pressure
- [x] Benchmarks and dashboard snapshots attached
- [x] Config + docs + changelog

Why this approach: Prior attempts (pure LRU or size-only eviction) either left many fragmented blocks scattered across the slab allocator or evicted many small hot entries causing quality regressions. Adaptive compaction reduces fragmentation surface area before eviction; priority-based eviction reduces unnecessary paging by preferring large fragmented entries that free contiguous blocks for allocation. Background spillover reduces latencies for critical request paths.

Backwards compatibility & safety: All features are behind runtime flags and defaults tuned to conservative values. Compaction runs in background threads and is interruptible; eviction order can be toggled back to legacy LRU via config. No on-disk format changes to existing spill files (backwards compatible).

Related tickets: ENG-1294 (KV cache compaction design), ENG-1320 (paging telemetry), SUP-421 (customer incident involving spill latency).

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can you clarify compaction impact on CPU during peak inference? We need a bound so autoscaler doesn't spike. Author: Compaction is rate limited and uses a cooperative yield; added config kv.compaction_cpu_limit and a note in docs. Also added a bench to measure CPU when compaction runs (results in bench_results).

Daniel Kim: Is eviction priority deterministic across restarts (important for reproducible tests)? Author: Score incorporates stable id + timestamp; added a deterministic fallback path in tests and documented it. See tests/unit/test_eviction_priority.rs for deterministic test harness.

Linus Ortega: The spill writer could cause head-of-line blocking on shutdown. Can we ensure graceful drain? Author: Added shutdown draining with timeout and safe abort; updated spill_writer to flush on shutdown and moved sync barrier to background worker.
release_notes: Improves KV cache fragmentation handling and reduces paging/spillover under mixed-context workloads. Adds adaptive compaction and priority-aware eviction. Exposes tuning knobs under kv.* configs. No breaking changes by default.
bench_results: Local canary (gpu-a100, mixed workload): 8-12% throughput improvement at 95th percentile concurrency
Paging events: observed 15% reduction in synchronous page faults in synthetic mixed-context benchmark
Memory footprint: 6-9% reduction in peak GPU memory usage due to reduced fragmentation
notes: Feature gated by kv.compaction_enabled (default: true conservative), kv.eviction_mode (legacy|priority). Rollout plan: gradual canary -> cluster-wide after 48h observation.
